name: Nativism (politics)
summary: A political stance that favours established inhabitants over immigrants and holds that a state should belong to its native group. In Cas Mudde's definition it is a xenophobic form of nationalism that treats non-native people and ideas as a threat, and its modern form stresses protecting cultural heritage, reserving jobs and welfare for citizens and requiring assimilation.
scope: Nativism as the sources define the name: the view that a state should belong to its native group and that non-native people and ideas threaten it (Mudde; Britannica), in two strands: the American nativism of the 1840s-50s (Native American and American "Know Nothing" Party, its 1855 principles and 1856 platform) and the modern nativism Mudde treats as the dominant feature of the populist radical right. Authoritarianism, populism and the rest of the far-right package count only where a defining source ties them to nativism, so economic, government-structure and most other statements are null.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Mudde states that the nativist aim is to give non-natives a choice between assimilation, that is becoming native, and repatriation.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Mudde says nativists almost always argue or imply that the native culture is superior, although some use the neutral language of ethnopluralism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Mudde defines nativism as holding that non-native persons and ideas are fundamentally threatening to the homogeneous nation-state.

elite-replacement.rationale: Mudde reports that populist radical right nativists believe mass immigration is organised by progressive politicians, and Britannica says many nativists have embraced replacement theory; not all strands do.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mudde defines nativism as the view that states should be inhabited exclusively by the native group (the nation) and calls its ultimate goal an ethnocracy, where citizenship rests on ethnicity.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Plank 8 of the 1856 platform says no State or Territory ought to admit others than citizens to the right of suffrage; it does not name local elections separately.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Plank 9 of the 1856 American Party platform demands twenty-one years of continued residence as an indispensable requisite for citizenship.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The 1855 American Party statement of principles charges that Catholics seek power to mould or subvert American institutions, and the Know Nothings feared a papal plot; modern nativists allege elite plots.

native-born-offices.rationale: Plank 3 of the 1856 American Party platform says "Americans must rule America" and that native-born citizens should be selected for all offices in preference to all others.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The 1855 statement says the party would oppose any religious denomination detected bringing its members into political combination, so politics should not be organised by denomination.

open-borders.rationale: Mudde states the nativist goal of a homogeneous state is reached by closing the borders to immigrants, which contradicts eventually open borders.

population-transfer.rationale: Mudde says those non-natives unwilling to assimilate must be expelled to the country they or their ancestors came from, since non-native elements are seen as fundamentally threatening.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Britannica says nativist opposition to immigration is expressed as concern to preserve national, cultural or religious identity, and Mudde has nativists treating non-native ideas as threats to the nation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Britannica defines nativism as prioritising native-born residents over immigrants "typically by advocating or enacting restrictions on immigration", and Mudde says it aims to close the borders to immigrants.

right-to-secede.rationale: Plank 2 of the 1856 platform calls for the perpetuation of the Federal Union; the modern strand sources are silent.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 1856 platform opposes any union between Church and State and the 1855 principles hold even a slight union dangerous to both; the sources on the modern strand are silent.

missingStatements.text: Immigrants should have to live in a country for many years before they can become citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform demanded 21 years of residence for citizenship, and nativists have repeatedly sought longer naturalization waits.

notes: Rules 7 pass: every earlier answer re-checked; those that rested on a general stance, on the wider populist radical right, or on the fact that a view is unrelated to nativism were nulled (history kept). Themes searched: immigration, citizenship, culture and language, religion and church-state, elites and conspiracy, offices and suffrage, federalism; economy, welfare, trade, ecology, technology and gender are not stated in the defining sources. Whether the native group is defined by ethnicity, culture or religion varies by strand; Mudde notes some nativists use ethnopluralist language and others racial language.
